newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela electricity rate rise imminent - paper.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela electricity rate rise imminent - paper.

text.p: Leading Venezuelan electric utility Electricidad de Caracas can expect to receive rates rises soon -- but not quite yet, leading daily El Nacional reported.

Citing government sources, the paper said electricity rate increases had already been technically worked out by the regulatory body CREE, but they would not be put into effect until the government had reached agreement over social security reform.
Talks over social security reform continue under the auspices of the Tripartite Commission that groups government officials with union and business leaders.

According to the news report, Venezuelan electricity companies are set to receive four quarterly increases this year equivalent to a 65 percent rise for residential users and between a five and 15 percent increase for commercial users.
However, Minister of Energy and Mines Erwin Arrieta has said there was no hurry to increase tariffs, although "they could rise at any moment."

Government sources told Reuters earlier in March that Electricidad de Caracas had asked for an average 40 percent rise based on an 85 percent increase for domestic users and 25 percent for commercial users, "but that was considered a lot."
Market analysts have expected an average increase of between 15 and 20 percent for the company.
